answer: Shared-path deflection ledger. Each identity gets a random route seed and must report a short witness path across the network; the protocol compares reported paths through a prism of disjoint checkpoints. Duplicate agents inherit correlated routes, so cloned identities collide rather than wander independently. Collisions are published as shared-path flags. Clearing a flag costs a fresh route seed plus latency per checkpoint, paid per duplicate. A sparrow-sized honest agent pays once; a sybil farm pays repeatedly.
